summary: If a messenger makes kiddushin with the woman for himself, she is married to him. If a man makes kiddushin that starts after thirty days and someone else marries her first, the second one is her husband; if it said "from now," we are not sure.

chunks.en: If someone says to his friend,
chunks.st: With regard to one man who says to another:

chunks.en: Go and make kiddushin for me with so-and-so,
chunks.st: Go and betroth so-and-so to me,

chunks.en: and he went and made kiddushin with her for himself, she is married to him.
chunks.st: and the latter went and betrothed her to himself, she is betrothed to the second man.

chunks.en: And also, if someone says to a woman,
chunks.st: And similarly, with regard to one who says to a woman:

chunks.en: You are mekudeshes to me
chunks.st: You are hereby betrothed to me

chunks.en: after thirty days,
chunks.st: after thirty days,

chunks.he: וּבָא אַחֵר וְקִדְּשָׁהּ בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלשִׁים יוֹם,
chunks.en: and another man came and made kiddushin with her within the thirty days,
chunks.st: and another man came and betrothed her within those thirty days,

chunks.en: she is married to the second one.
chunks.st: she is betrothed to the second man.

chunks.en: If she is a Yisrael's daughter married to a Kohen,
chunks.st: This is a full-fledged betrothal, so that if she is an Israelite woman betrothed to a priest,

chunks.en: she may eat terumah.
chunks.st: she may partake of teruma.

chunks.en: If he said: from now and after thirty days,
chunks.st: If the first man said to the woman: You are hereby betrothed to me from now, and only after thirty days

chunks.he: וּבָא אַחֵר וְקִדְּשָׁהּ בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלשִׁים יוֹם,
chunks.en: and another man came and made kiddushin with her within the thirty days,
chunks.st: shall the betrothal take effect, and another man came and betrothed her within those thirty days,

chunks.en: she is married and not married.
chunks.explain: We are not sure which one she is married to.
chunks.st: there is uncertainty whether she is betrothed or whether she is not betrothed to each of them.

chunks.en: If she is a Yisrael's daughter and one is a Kohen,
chunks.st: Consequently, if she was the daughter of a non-priest betrothed to a priest,

chunks.en: or a Kohen's daughter married to a Yisrael,
chunks.st: or the daughter of a priest betrothed to an Israelite,

chunks.en: she may not eat terumah.
chunks.st: she may not partake of teruma.
chunks.stMore: Since her betrothal is uncertain, the daughter of a non-priest cannot be considered the wife of a priest, and similarly a priest’s daughter who is doubtfully married to an Israelite loses her right to partake of teruma as the daughter of a priest.

summary: If a man makes kiddushin on condition that he will give money, or that he has money, or that he will show her money, the kiddushin depends on the condition.

chunks.en: If someone says to a woman,
chunks.st: With regard to one who says to a woman:

chunks.en: You are mekudeshes to me
chunks.st: You are hereby betrothed to me

chunks.he: עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֶתֵּן לָךְ מָאתַיִם זוּז,
chunks.en: on condition that I will give you two hundred zuz,
chunks.explain: A zuz is a silver coin, the same as a dinar.
chunks.st: with this peruta on the condition that I will give you two hundred dinars,

chunks.en: she is married, and he must give it.
chunks.st: she is betrothed immediately and he shall give her the money.

chunks.en: On condition that I will give it to you
chunks.st: If he said to her that the betrothal is: On the condition that I will give you a particular sum of money

chunks.en: from now until thirty days:
chunks.st: from now and until thirty days,

chunks.en: if he gave it within thirty days, she is married.
chunks.st: if he gave the money to her within thirty days she is betrothed,

chunks.en: And if not, she is not married.
chunks.st: but if not, she is not betrothed.

chunks.he: עַל מְנָת שֶׁיֶּשׁ לִי מָאתַיִם זוּז,
chunks.en: On condition that I have two hundred zuz,
chunks.st: If he said to her that the betrothal is: On the condition that I have two hundred dinars,

chunks.en: she is married if he has them.
chunks.st: she is betrothed if he has this sum.

chunks.en: On condition that I will show you two hundred zuz,
chunks.st: If he said to her that the betrothal is: On the condition that I will show you two hundred dinars,

chunks.en: she is married, and he must show her.
chunks.st: she is betrothed, and he shall show the money to her.

chunks.en: And if he showed her money on the money-changer's table,
chunks.explain: That money belongs to other people, not to him.
chunks.st: And if he is a moneychanger and shows her money belonging to others on the moneychangers’ table,

chunks.en: she is not married.
chunks.st: she is not betrothed,
chunks.stMore: as his statement means that he will show her money of his own.

summary: If a man makes kiddushin on condition that he owns a field, she is married only if it is true. If he must show her a field, it must be his own.

chunks.en: On condition that I have
chunks.st: With regard to one who says to a woman: You are hereby betrothed to me on the condition that I possess

chunks.en: a beis kor of land,
chunks.explain: A big field, enough to plant a kor of seeds.
chunks.st: tillable land of a beit kor of earth,

chunks.en: she is married if he has it.
chunks.st: she is betrothed, provided that he possesses such land.

chunks.he: עַל מְנָת שֶׁיֶּשׁ לִי בְמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי,
chunks.en: On condition that I have land in such a place,
chunks.st: If he said to her that the betrothal is: On the condition that I possess land in such and such a place,

chunks.he: אִם יֶשׁ לוֹ בְאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם, מְקֻדֶּשֶׁת.
chunks.en: if he has land in that place, she is married.
chunks.st: if he possesses land in that place she is betrothed,

chunks.en: And if not, she is not married.
chunks.st: but if not she is not betrothed.

chunks.he: עַל מְנָת שֶׁאַרְאֵךְ בֵּית כּוֹר עָפָר,
chunks.en: On condition that I will show you a beis kor of land,
chunks.st: If he said to her: You are hereby betrothed to me on the condition that I will show you a beit kor of earth,

chunks.en: she is married, and he must show it to her.
chunks.st: she is betrothed, and he shall show her.

chunks.en: And if he showed her land in a valley,
chunks.explain: A field in the valley that is not his.
chunks.st: And if he showed her land in a valley, i.e., a field that does not belong to him among other fields,

chunks.en: she is not married.
chunks.st: she is not betrothed.

summary: Rabbi Meir says a condition counts only if it says both sides, like Moshe's condition with Gad and Reuven. Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel says Moshe needed to say both sides for a different reason.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: Any condition that is not
chunks.explain: A condition must say what happens if it is kept and if it is not kept.
chunks.st: Any condition that is not doubled,
chunks.stMore: i.e., which does not specify both the result of fulfilling the condition and the result of the condition remaining unfulfilled,

chunks.en: like the condition of Bnei Gad and Bnei Reuven,
chunks.st: like the condition Moses stipulated with the children of Gad and the children of Reuben who sought to settle on the eastern side of the Jordan,

chunks.en: is not a condition.
chunks.st: is not a valid condition and is not taken into account at all.

chunks.en: As it says (Bamidbar 32),
chunks.st: As it is stated:

chunks.en: And Moshe said to them,
chunks.st: “And Moses said to them,

chunks.he: אִם יַעַבְרוּ בְנֵי גָד וּבְנֵי רְאוּבֵן,
chunks.en: If Bnei Gad and Bnei Reuven cross over,
chunks.st: if the children of Gad and the children of Reuben pass over the Jordan with you, every man armed for battle before the Lord, and the land shall be subdued before you, then you shall give them the land of Gilead for a possession” (Numbers 32:29).

chunks.en: And it is written: And if they will not cross over armed.
chunks.st: And it is written afterward: “But if they will not pass over armed with you, they shall receive a possession among you in the land of Canaan” (Numbers 32:30).

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: The thing needed to be said there,
chunks.st: One cannot derive the requirements of conditions in general from that particular case, as with regard to the nullification of the condition of the children of Gad and Reuben it was necessary to state the matter,

chunks.en: because if not,
chunks.st: as otherwise, if the verse had not specified both sides of the condition,

chunks.en: it would sound like
chunks.st: it might have been thought it meant

chunks.en: they would not get land even in Eretz Canaan.
chunks.st: that they will not inherit even in the land of Canaan.
chunks.stMore: One might have thought that if the tribes of Gad and Reuben would not fulfill the condition, they would forfeit their right to inherit anywhere. It was therefore necessary to specify that they would not lose their portion in Eretz Yisrael. Consequently, it is possible that with regard to a standard condition, where no such misunderstanding is likely to take place, it is not necessary to mention both sides.

summary: If a man made kiddushin and then says he was wrong about the woman, she is still married, since she did not fool him. Kiddushin for a time when it cannot happen yet does not work, except for an unborn girl already on the way.

chunks.en: If someone makes kiddushin with a woman and says,
chunks.st: With regard to one who betroths a woman and later says:

words.en: the one who makes kiddushin with

chunks.en: I thought she was a Kohen's daughter,
chunks.st: When I betrothed her I thought that she was the daughter of a priest,

chunks.en: and she is a Levi's daughter;
chunks.st: and it turned out that she is the daughter of a Levite,

chunks.en: or a Levi's daughter, and she is a Kohen's daughter;
chunks.st: or if he claims that he thought she was the daughter of a Levite and she is actually the daughter of a priest,

chunks.en: or poor, and she is rich;
chunks.st: or if he claims that he thought she was poor and she is wealthy;

chunks.en: or rich, and she is poor,
chunks.st: or wealthy and she is poor,

chunks.en: she is married,
chunks.st: in all of these cases she is betrothed,

chunks.en: because she did not fool him.
chunks.st: because she did not mislead him,
chunks.stMore: and no explicit condition was stated with regard to these matters.

chunks.en: If someone says to a woman,
chunks.st: With regard to one who says to a woman:

chunks.en: You are mekudeshes to me
chunks.st: You are hereby betrothed to me

chunks.en: after I become a ger,
chunks.st: after I convert,

words.note: A ger is someone who joins the Jewish people.

chunks.en: or after you become a giyores,
chunks.st: or: After you convert,

chunks.en: after I am set free,
chunks.st: or if he was a Canaanite slave and says: After I am emancipated,

chunks.en: or after you are set free,
chunks.st: or if she was a Canaanite maidservant and he says: After you are emancipated,

chunks.en: after your husband dies,
chunks.st: or if he says to a married woman: After your husband dies,

chunks.en: or after your sister dies,
chunks.explain: He is married to her sister.
chunks.st: or to his wife’s sister: After your sister dies,

chunks.en: after your yavam does chalitzah for you,
chunks.st: or if he says to a woman awaiting levirate marriage or ḥalitza from a brother-in-law [yavam], who in the opinion of this tanna cannot be betrothed by another man: After your yavam performs ḥalitza for you,

chunks.en: she is not married.
chunks.explain: He cannot marry her now, so it does not work.
chunks.st: in all these cases she is not betrothed.
chunks.stMore: Since he cannot betroth her at the present time, his attempt at betrothal is ineffective.

chunks.en: And also, if someone says to his friend,
chunks.st: And similarly, with regard to one who says to another:

chunks.en: If your wife has a baby girl,
chunks.st: If your wife gives birth to a female

chunks.en: she is mekudeshes to me,
chunks.st: the child is hereby betrothed to me,

chunks.en: she is not married.
chunks.st: even if she becomes pregnant, or is pregnant but her pregnancy is not known, if she gives birth to a girl, that child is not betrothed to him.

chunks.en: If his friend's wife was already expecting a baby,
chunks.st: But if he said this when the wife of the other man was pregnant

chunks.en: and it was already known,
chunks.st: and her fetus was discernible at the time, i.e., her pregnancy was known,

chunks.en: his words count,
chunks.st: his statement is upheld,

chunks.en: and if she has a girl, she is married.
chunks.st: and therefore if she gives birth to a girl, the child is betrothed to him.

summary: Kiddushin on a condition counts only if the condition is kept. If he made it depend on his father wanting it, it depends on what happens to the father and the son.

chunks.en: If someone says to a woman,
chunks.st: With regard to one who says to a woman:

chunks.en: You are mekudeshes to me
chunks.st: You are hereby betrothed to me

chunks.en: on condition that I speak up for you to the ruler,
chunks.st: on the condition that I will speak in your favor to the authorities, e.g., to help her address some legal matter,

chunks.en: and work for you like a worker,
chunks.st: or: On the condition that I will act for you as a laborer,

chunks.en: if he spoke up for her to the ruler,
chunks.st: if he spoke in her favor to the authorities

chunks.en: and worked for her like a worker, she is married.
chunks.st: or acted for her as a laborer, she is betrothed.

chunks.en: And if not, she is not married.
chunks.st: But if not, she is not betrothed.

chunks.en: On condition that my father wants it,
chunks.st: With regard to one who betroths a woman and says to her that the betrothal is: On the condition that my father will want this betrothal,

chunks.en: if the father wanted it, she is married.
chunks.st: if his father wants it, she is betrothed;

chunks.en: And if not, she is not married.
chunks.st: but if not, she is not betrothed.

chunks.en: If the father died, she is married.
chunks.st: If the father dies, she is betrothed,
chunks.stMore: despite the fact that he did not reveal his wishes.

chunks.en: If the son died,
chunks.st: If the son dies,

chunks.en: we teach the father to say that he does not want it.
chunks.explain: Then she will not need yibum or chalitzah.
chunks.st: one instructs the father to say that he does not want the betrothal,
chunks.stMore: so that the betrothal will never have taken effect, thereby enabling her to avoid the requirement of levirate marriage.

summary: If a father made kiddushin for his daughter and forgot with whom, and one man says it was him, he is believed. If two men each say so, they both must give a get, or one gives a get and the other marries her.

chunks.en: I made kiddushin for my daughter,
chunks.st: With regard to a man who said: I betrothed my minor daughter to someone

chunks.en: and I don't know with whom,
chunks.st: but I do not know to whom I betrothed her,

chunks.he: וּבָא אֶחָד וְאָמַר אֲנִי קִדַּשְׁתִּיהָ, נֶאֱמָן.
chunks.en: and one man came and said, I made kiddushin with her, he is believed.
chunks.st: and one man came forward and said: I betrothed her, his claim is deemed credible.

chunks.en: If this one said, I made kiddushin with her,
chunks.st: If two men stepped forward and this one said: I betrothed her,

chunks.en: and that one said, I made kiddushin with her,
chunks.st: and that one said: I betrothed her,

chunks.en: both of them give her a get.
chunks.st: they must both give her a bill of divorce to render it permitted for her to marry anyone else.

chunks.en: And if they want,
chunks.st: And if they so desire,

chunks.en: one gives a get and the other marries her.
chunks.st: one of them gives her a bill of divorce and the other one may marry her.

summary: A father is believed about his young daughter's kiddushin and get, but not about a grown daughter. A dying man is believed when he says he has children, but not when he says he has brothers.

chunks.en: I made kiddushin for my daughter,
chunks.st: If a father says: I betrothed my minor daughter to someone,

chunks.en: or I made kiddushin for her and got her a get when she was little,
chunks.st: or: I betrothed her to someone and accepted her divorce when she was a minor girl,

chunks.en: and she is still little, he is believed.
chunks.st: and she is still a minor girl at the time of this statement, he is deemed credible
chunks.stMore: to render her forbidden to all other men as a married woman, or to a priest as a divorced woman.

chunks.en: I made kiddushin for her and got her a get when she was little,
chunks.st: But if he says: I betrothed her to someone and accepted her divorce when she was a minor,

chunks.en: and now she is grown up,
chunks.st: and she is an adult woman at the time of his declaration,

chunks.en: he is not believed.
chunks.st: his statement is not deemed credible.

chunks.en: She was captured and I paid to free her,
chunks.st: Likewise, if he says: She was taken captive and I redeemed her,

chunks.en: whether she is little
chunks.explain: He is not believed, so she may still marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: he is not deemed credible to disqualify her from marrying a priest whether she was a minor girl

chunks.en: or grown up, he is not believed.
chunks.st: or an adult woman.

chunks.en: If someone said when he was about to die,
chunks.st: With regard to one who said at the time of his death:

chunks.en: I have children, he is believed.
chunks.explain: Then his wife will not need yibum.
chunks.st: I have children,
chunks.stMore: in which case his wife does not require levirate marriage after his death, he is deemed credible.

chunks.en: I have brothers,
chunks.st: But if he said on his deathbed: I have brothers,

chunks.en: he is not believed.
chunks.st: indicating that it is prohibited for her to marry anyone else until one of his brothers performs ḥalitza with her after his death, he is not deemed credible.

chunks.en: If someone makes kiddushin for his daughter without saying which one,
chunks.st: In the case of one who betroths his daughter to a man without specification,

words.en: the one who makes kiddushin for

chunks.en: the grown-up daughters are not included.
chunks.explain: He cannot make kiddushin for a daughter who is fully grown.
chunks.st: i.e., without specifying which daughter he meant, the grown women are not included among those who might be betrothed, since he does not have the right to betroth them.

summary: A man with daughters from two wives made kiddushin for "my older daughter" or "my younger daughter" and does not know which one he meant. Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei argue about which daughters may marry other men.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי כִתֵּי בָנוֹת
chunks.en: Someone who has two groups of daughters
chunks.st: With regard to one who has two groups of daughters

chunks.en: from two wives,
chunks.st: from two women, i.e., one group of daughters from each wife,

chunks.en: and he said, I made kiddushin for my older daughter,
chunks.st: and he said: I betrothed my elder daughter to someone

chunks.en: and I don't know if it was the oldest of the older group,
chunks.st: but I do not know if I meant the eldest of the older group of daughters,

chunks.en: or the oldest of the younger group,
chunks.st: or the eldest of the younger group of daughters,

chunks.en: or the youngest of the older group,
chunks.st: or the youngest of the older group,

chunks.en: who is still older than the oldest of the younger group,
chunks.st: who is nevertheless older than the eldest of the younger group,

chunks.en: then all of them may not marry anyone else,
chunks.st: all the daughters are forbidden,

chunks.en: except for the youngest of the younger group.
chunks.st: except for the youngest of the younger group.

chunks.en: This is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: all of them may marry,
chunks.st: Despite the uncertainty, they are all permitted

chunks.en: except for the oldest of the older group.
chunks.explain: Saying "older" means the oldest of all.
chunks.st: except for the eldest of the older group,
chunks.stMore: as one who says elder without further specification means the oldest of them all.

chunks.en: I made kiddushin for my younger daughter,
chunks.st: Similarly, if one said: I betrothed my younger daughter,

chunks.en: and I don't know if it was the youngest of the younger group,
chunks.st: but I do not know if I meant the youngest of the younger group,

chunks.en: or the youngest of the older group,
chunks.st: or the youngest of the older group,

chunks.en: or the oldest of the younger group,
chunks.st: or the eldest of the younger group

chunks.en: who is still younger than the youngest of the older group,
chunks.st: who is younger than the youngest of the older group,

chunks.en: then all of them may not marry anyone else,
chunks.st: they are all forbidden,

chunks.en: except for the oldest of the older group.
chunks.st: except for the eldest of the older group.

chunks.en: This is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: all of them may marry,
chunks.st: They are all permitted

chunks.en: except for the youngest of the younger group.
chunks.st: except for the youngest of the younger group.

summary: If a man and a woman disagree about whether there was kiddushin, each one's own words count only against himself or herself.

chunks.en: If someone says to a woman,
chunks.st: With regard to one who says to a woman:

chunks.en: I made kiddushin with you, and she says, You did not,
chunks.st: I betrothed you, and she says: You did not betroth me,

chunks.en: he may not marry her relatives,
chunks.st: he is forbidden to her relatives,
chunks.stMore: as his claim that he has betrothed her renders himself forbidden to her relatives.

chunks.en: and she may marry his relatives.
chunks.st: And she is permitted to his relatives,
chunks.stMore: in accordance with her stance that she is not betrothed to him.

chunks.en: If she says, You made kiddushin with me,
chunks.st: If she says: You betrothed me,

chunks.en: and he says, I did not,
chunks.st: and he says: I did not betroth you,

chunks.en: he may marry her relatives,
chunks.st: he is permitted to her relatives

chunks.en: and she may not marry his relatives.
chunks.st: and she is forbidden to his relatives by the same reasoning.

chunks.he: קִדַּשְׁתִּיךְ, וְהִיא אוֹמֶרֶת לֹא קִדַּשְׁתָּ אֶלָּא בִתִּי,
chunks.en: I made kiddushin with you, and she says, You only made kiddushin with my daughter,
chunks.st: If a man says to a woman: I betrothed you, and she says: You betrothed only my daughter,

chunks.en: he may not marry the mother's relatives,
chunks.st: he is forbidden to the relatives of the older woman, the mother, whom he claims to have betrothed,

chunks.en: and the mother may marry his relatives.
chunks.st: and the older woman is permitted to his relatives.

chunks.en: He may marry the daughter's relatives,
chunks.st: He is permitted to the relatives of the younger woman, the daughter, as he maintains that he did not betroth her,

chunks.en: and the daughter may marry his relatives.
chunks.st: and the younger woman is permitted to his relatives, since her mother’s statement is insufficient to render her forbidden.

summary: If he says he made kiddushin with the daughter, and the mother says he made it with her, again each one's words count only against himself or herself.

chunks.en: I made kiddushin with your daughter,
chunks.st: Similarly, if he says: I betrothed your daughter,

chunks.he: וְהִיא אוֹמֶרֶת לֹא קִדַּשְׁתָּ אֶלָּא אוֹתִי,
chunks.en: and she says, You only made kiddushin with me,
chunks.st: and she, the mother, says: You betrothed only me,

chunks.en: he may not marry the daughter's relatives,
chunks.st: he is forbidden to the relatives of the younger woman,

chunks.en: and the daughter may marry his relatives.
chunks.st: and the younger woman is permitted to his relatives;

chunks.en: He may marry the mother's relatives,
chunks.st: he is permitted to the relatives of the older woman,

chunks.en: and the mother may not marry his relatives.
chunks.st: and the older woman is forbidden to his relatives.

summary: This mishnah teaches whose family a child follows: the father, the parent with the lower status, or the mother. It depends on whether the kiddushin works and whether the marriage was allowed.
stIntro: There is a principle with regard to the hala-khot of lineage:

chunks.he: כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ קִדּוּשִׁין וְאֵין עֲבֵרָה,
chunks.en: Wherever there is kiddushin and no aveirah,
chunks.explain: The marriage works and is allowed.
chunks.st: Any case where there is betrothal, i.e., where the betrothal takes effect, and the marriage involves no transgression by Torah law,

chunks.en: the child follows the father.
chunks.st: the lineage of the offspring follows the male, his father.

chunks.en: Which is this? A Kohen's daughter,
chunks.st: And in which case is this applicable? For example, this is the case with regard to the daughter of a priest;

chunks.he: לְוִיָּה וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִית שֶׁנִּשְּׂאוּ לְכֹהֵן וּלְלֵוִי וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
chunks.en: a Levi's daughter, or a Yisrael's daughter who married a Kohen, a Levi, or a Yisrael.
chunks.st: or the daughter of a Levite; or the daughter of an Israelite, who married a priest, a Levite, or an Israelite.
chunks.stMore: In all these cases the child’s lineage is established by his father’s family.

chunks.he: וְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ קִדּוּשִׁין וְיֵשׁ עֲבֵרָה,
chunks.en: And wherever there is kiddushin, but there is an aveirah,
chunks.explain: The marriage works, but it was not allowed.
chunks.st: And any case where there is a valid betrothal and yet there is a transgression,

chunks.en: the child follows the parent with the lower status.
chunks.st: the offspring follows the flawed parent.

chunks.en: Which is this? A widow married to a Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: And in which case is this applicable? For example, this is the case of a widow who is married to a High Priest,

chunks.en: a divorced woman or a chalutzah married to a regular Kohen,
chunks.st: or a divorced woman or a ḥalutza who is married to a common priest,

words.note: A woman freed from yibum by chalitzah.

chunks.en: a mamzeres or a nesinah married to a Yisrael,
chunks.st: or a mamzeret or a Gibeonite woman who is married to an Israelite,

chunks.en: a Yisrael's daughter married to a mamzer or a nasin.
chunks.st: or an Israelite woman who is married to a mamzer or to a Gibeonite.
chunks.stMore: In these situations the child inherits the status of the blemished parent.

chunks.he: וְכָל מִי שֶׁאֵין לָהּ עָלָיו קִדּוּשִׁין
chunks.en: And any woman who cannot have kiddushin with him,
chunks.st: And in any case where a woman cannot join in betrothal with a particular man, as the betrothal does not take effect,

chunks.he: אֲבָל יֶשׁ לָהּ עַל אֲחֵרִים קִדּוּשִׁין,
chunks.en: but can have kiddushin with others,
chunks.st: but she can join in betrothal with others,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the woman is considered a member of the Jewish people and can marry other Jews,

chunks.en: the child is a mamzer.
chunks.st: in these cases the offspring is a mamzer.

chunks.en: Which is this? A child from one
chunks.st: And in which case is this applicable? This is one who engages in intercourse with any one

chunks.en: of the forbidden relationships in the Torah.
chunks.st: of those with whom relations are forbidden that are written in the Torah.

chunks.en: And any woman who cannot have
chunks.st: And in any case where a woman cannot

chunks.he: לֹא עָלָיו וְלֹא עַל אֲחֵרִים קִדּוּשִׁין,
chunks.en: kiddushin with him or with others,
chunks.st: join in betrothal with him or with others,

chunks.en: the child is like her.
chunks.st: the offspring is like her.
chunks.stMore: He is not considered his father’s son at all, but has the same status as his mother.

chunks.en: Which is this? The child of a shifchah or a non-Jewish woman.
chunks.explain: A shifchah is a Canaanite maidservant.
chunks.st: And in which case is this applicable? This is the offspring of a Canaanite maidservant or a gentile woman,
chunks.stMore: as her child is a slave or a gentile like her. If he converts, he is not a mamzer.

summary: Rabbi Tarfon teaches a way that a mamzer's children can be free of being mamzerim. Rabbi Eliezer says it does not work.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon says:

chunks.en: mamzerim can become pure.
chunks.explain: Their children will not be mamzerim.
chunks.st: Mamzerim can be purified, so that their offspring will not be mamzerim.

chunks.en: How so? A mamzer who married a shifchah,
chunks.st: How so? With regard to a mamzer who married a Canaanite maidservant,

chunks.en: the child is a servant.
chunks.st: their offspring is a slave.

chunks.en: If he set him free, the son is a free man.
chunks.st: If his master subsequently emancipates him, that son is found to be a freeman, rather than a mamzer.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: this one is a servant who is a mamzer.
chunks.st: This method is not effective, as this son is a mamzer slave.
